name: Smoke Bridge

steps.text: Plug the Smoke Bridge into an unswitched wall outlet near the First Alert alarm.
Press and hold the SET button until the Smoke Bridge beeps.
Within four minutes, press and hold the First Alert alarm's test button until it beeps or says "testing".
steps.expect: Smoke Bridge LED blinks red while the alarm sends its test messages, then stops

steps.text: Test the pairing by pressing and holding the First Alert alarm's test button again.
steps.expect: Smoke Bridge LED blinks red until the message ends

notes: Requires a First Alert ONELINK smoke and CO alarm.
The Smoke Bridge doesn't receive wireless RF signals from Insteon devices.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Smoke Bridge beeps.

notes: Then adjust the responder to the state you want and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps. The Smoke Bridge double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

Test by setting the responder to a different state and tapping the Smoke Bridge's SET button; it cycles through smoke, CO, low battery, error and all clear. Links made with the SET button respond only to smoke detected; use software for the other groups.
The Smoke Bridge is a controller only.
If either device's LED keeps blinking, the link failed; tap its SET button until the LED stops and try again.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the Smoke Bridge beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Smoke Bridge beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the scene state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button to finish.
Press and hold the SET button until the Smoke Bridge beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the Smoke Bridge double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
For several responders, tap the SET button after the LED blinks red (it double-blinks red), press and hold each responder's SET button until it double-beeps, then tap the SET button to finish.

steps.text: Unplug the Smoke Bridge.
Wait 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging the Smoke Bridge back in; don't let go.
When the long beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds, a double beep

steps.text: Pair the Smoke Bridge with the First Alert alarm again.

notes: Erases all settings and scenes, including the pairing with the First Alert alarm.

steps.text: Remove the Smoke Bridge as a controller from each of its responders.
Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the Smoke Bridge 2982-222 Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: It sends Insteon messages over powerline only; its radio only listens for the smoke alarms it's paired with.
Tapping its SET button sends each group's command as a test, ending with the all-clear.
It sends a heartbeat to group 10 (0x0A) about once every 24 hours, which software can turn off.
Group 4 is the all-clear on earlier firmware and a new or unknown alarm on later firmware.
